finding: The repaired v0.36.0 row is false on both of its numbers and contradicts two other sections of the same spec. The cell reads '13, converged' and 'converges under all | round 13'. Measured from spec/.tp-review/0.36.0/state.json, all 13 recorded audit rounds carry clean:false -- that cycle has never converged under the rule tp ships today, which is exactly the `all` predicate. Per-round surviving non-PASS rows (no audit row anywhere in the corpus carries a `resolved` key, so surviving == non-PASS): r8 3, r9 4, r10 2, r11 1, r12 2 (both error), r13 3 (2 error, 1 warning). With audit_clean_rounds: 2, `all` needs two consecutive zero-surviving rounds and v0.36.0 never reaches even one, so 'round 13' is unreachable rather than merely optimistic. §2.0a says the opposite of the cell in plain words -- 'consecutive_clean never left zero' -- and §2's own opening says rounds 7, 12 and 13 carry error rows, which cannot coexist with round 13 being an `all`-convergence. The row is load-bearing twice: it is half of 'the two cycles disagree', and it is the evidence for '`all` reproduces the recorded history exactly', which holds only for v0.35.0 (r8 and r9 are the only zero-surviving audit rounds in either cycle).
suggestion: Replace the cell with the measured outcome -- 'never converges under `all`; 13 rounds recorded, none clean' -- and scope the 'reproduces the recorded history exactly' claim to v0.35.0. If the column actually means 'the round the phase stopped at', rename it, because v0.36.0's stop was an operator decision rather than a predicate firing; and add the v0.36.0 replay to §7 test 4 so the cell is pinned by an assertion rather than by prose.

finding: The round-1 repair landed in §2 and was not propagated to §2.1, so the two adjacent sections now hand the decision-maker opposite tallies of the same evidence. §2 concludes 'the instrument scores 2 of 2 cycles in which `blocking` would have shipped over an `error` row, not 1 of 2'. §2.1's summary is unchanged and still reads 'v0.35.0 is the case for the release', 'v0.36.0 is the case against the default', and 'the two cycles disagree, and one sample each way is not a policy'. Under §2's own corrected count the cycles do not disagree and there is no sample in favour, so §2.1's closing instruction to decomposition -- 'treat the default as the one decision in this release with a recorded argument against it' -- rests on a tally the same release withdrew two paragraphs earlier. This is not a wording clash: the surviving argument for shipping `blocking` as the default was the 1-1 split, and that split no longer exists in the spec.
suggestion: Rewrite §2.1's three summary paragraphs to the 2-of-2 reading, or delete them and let §2's paragraph carry the conclusion alone. Then re-argue §2's 'Default. blocking' against the corrected tally, or change the default, so the release does not ship a default whose only stated support has been retracted.

finding: §2 makes sink validation a normative deliverable -- 'This release therefore ships validation at the sink before the gate reads the field: a non-PASS row whose severity is missing or outside error | warning | info is rejected by --record the way an unknown category is' -- and calls it 'this release's first job'. §6 Non-Goal 3 states the opposite: 'Changing severity's meaning or vocabulary. error | warning | info is unchanged; this release only reads it.' Rejecting input at `tp audit --record` is not reading it; it changes what the command accepts and can refuse a round file that records cleanly today. No other section acknowledges the deliverable: §1 names two things the release gives audit, §5 closes 'This release is §2, §3 and §4', and §7's eight tests cover convergence, disposition and the streak reset only. The release's most safety-critical clause is thus the one its overview, its non-goals and its test list all contradict or omit.
suggestion: Give the validation its own numbered section carrying the mechanism, the exit code and the hint; add a §7 test for a rejected row and for an accepted one; and narrow Non-Goal 3 to 'the vocabulary is unchanged -- what changes is that it is now enforced at the sink'. Update §1 and §5's closing sentence to the same count.

finding: §2 prescribes two mutually exclusive dispositions for the same input and then admits the rule is unstated. One sentence rejects the row at `--record`; the next says 'The conservative rule for an unrecognised value must be stated normatively and must fail closed -- v0.31.0 §4.1 states its review counterpart that way and this section did not.' Rejection and fail-closed treatment are different behaviours with different blast radii: rejection refuses the round file so the row never enters the corpus, while fail-closed accepts the row and counts it as blocking. They also give opposite answers about the 67 historical rows §2 cites in the next paragraph -- unrecordable under rejection, uniformly blocking under fail-closed. §2 assigns those rows to a 'migration path' that no section of this release defines and §6 does not defer.
suggestion: Choose one rule and state it normatively in §2: either (a) `--record` rejects the row, with the exit code and hint named and an explicit statement that already-recorded rounds are untouched, or (b) the row is accepted and an unrecognised severity counts as blocking. Add the matching §7 test, and either specify the migration path for the 67 rows or list it as a Non-Goal with its reason.

finding: §2.0a assumes an audit-side `nonblocking_open`: 'audit_converge_on=blocking would have converged that run at round 3-4 with the remaining rows surfaced as nonblocking_open -- nothing hidden'. That field is documented as review-only and explicitly never an audit field. spec/0.31.0.md §8.4: 'nonblocking_open is review-only (audit convergence has no non-blocking notion, §4.4) and is never an audit field'; skills/tp/REFERENCE.md line 634 repeats it in the --compact disposition list; internal/cli/harness_note_test.go:263 records it in the audit --compact test's comment. This release is precisely what creates a non-blocking notion for audit, so emitting the field may be the right outcome -- but §2.0a treats it as an existing surface instead of specifying it. No section says when audit emits it or what it counts, §6 does not record the reversal of 0.31.0 §8.4, §7 has no test, and REFERENCE.md's --compact list would have to change. As written, the sentence that carries 'nothing hidden' -- the reassurance that makes stopping early acceptable -- depends on a surface the release does not ship.
suggestion: Either add a numbered clause specifying the audit-side emission on the same condition as review (a clean round with surviving non-blocking rows), a §7 test, and an explicit note that it supersedes spec/0.31.0.md §8.4's 'never an audit field'; or remove the field name from §2.0a and describe the outcome without naming a surface this release does not create.

finding: '§5 records the same gap from the --check side' no longer holds after §5 was rewritten. §5 now records that the --check divergence section was removed from this release and lives at spec/0.46.0.md §8; it states no gap of its own. A reader following the pointer for the substantive argument -- the one that says --check reports 'not converged' indefinitely while divergence gates nothing -- lands on a removal notice.
suggestion: Point the sentence at spec/0.46.0.md §8 directly, or drop it; §2.0a's own paragraph already makes the point.

finding: §2's opening paragraph reads 'it is the reason the sink validation above is a precondition rather than a nicety'. The sink validation is below it -- the paragraph beginning 'So the safety argument has to be built rather than cited' -- so the back-reference was written for the paragraph's earlier position and survived the round-1 repair that moved it to the top of §2. The same sentence's other pointer, 'The table below', is correct, which makes the wrong one easy to read past.
suggestion: Change 'above' to 'below', or move this summary paragraph to sit after the validation clause it summarises.

finding: §5 justifies the removal partly by length: the three sections 'added ~100 of 288 lines ... pushing it across the length threshold this repository measured as the strongest single predictor of cycle cost'. The removal did not restore the property it invokes. The spec is 229 lines, not the ~188 the arithmetic implies, because the same round grew §2 by roughly forty lines of narration about what round 1 falsified. CLAUDE.md's measurement is that specs under 200 lines cost ~8-9 total rounds and specs over 300 cost ~23; 229 is not in the cheap band, so the third bullet's remedy is asserted rather than achieved. The first two bullets (no mechanism, §5a inert) carry the removal on their own.
suggestion: Either drop the length bullet, or make it true by trimming §2's account of the round-1 repair -- the three-claim table and the corpus counts are the durable content; the narration of which draft said what is not.

finding: Near-miss, self-caught. I had concluded that §2's 'across recorded audit rows, 67 non-PASS rows carry out-of-enum severities (high 16, medium 15, low 36) in the v0.29.0-v0.32.0 cycles' was an instance of CLAUDE.md's uncounted-quantifier class, and was about to report it as an unbound measured constant in a paragraph whose neighbouring claims round 1 had already falsified. Counting every recorded audit row under spec/.tp-review/*/audit-round-*.ndjson before writing the row: 36 low, 15 medium, 16 high, total exactly 67, every one of them inside the stated range (0.29.0 3, 0.30.0 4, 0.31.0 2, 0.31.2 24, 0.32.0 34). The finding would have been false. Worth recording because the wrong conclusion was cheap to reach here -- three claims in the same paragraph were false last round, which makes the fourth feel false too.
suggestion: No spec change. This figure is the model for the rest of §2: a count reproducible from a named artifact, which is exactly what CLAUDE.md asks a quantifier to be.

finding: Near-miss, self-caught. While drafting the nonblocking_open finding I had concluded that an executable guard test pins 'nonblocking_open is never an audit field', and was about to cite it as a shipped assertion the spec silently reverses. Reading internal/cli/harness_note_test.go before writing: line 263 is a comment inside TestCompact_AuditOmitsHarnessKeepsNextAction, whose executable assertions cover harness_note, harness_stale and next_action only; every executable nonblocking_open assertion in the suite is review-side (harness_note_test.go:314/322, reviewconvergeon_clean_test.go:107/114, nextaction_test.go:60). The invariant is documented and commented, not asserted. The finding survives on the documentation (spec/0.31.0.md §8.4, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:634), but the citation I nearly wrote would have been wrong, and it is the kind of wrong that reads as stronger evidence than it is.
suggestion: Whichever way §2.0a's surface question is settled, add the executable assertion that comment stands in for -- absent on audit, or present under the stated condition.
